subsystems.name: Sample payload
subsystems.role: the biological material itself, prepared so it can survive decades of storage and one launch.
parts: desiccated seeds, spores and small organisms

subsystems.name: Storage vault
subsystems.role: holds the samples at a stable, sub-100 K temperature with as little active machinery as possible.

subsystems.name: Shielding
subsystems.role: keeps ionising radiation — the main damage pathway for DNA in cold storage — away from the samples.
parts: several metres of regolith overburden or lava-tube roof

subsystems.name: Robotic handling
subsystems.role: retrieves, inserts and inspects samples without warming them or letting them move between containers.

subsystems.name: Site services
subsystems.role: power, communications and the route between the surface and the vault.
parts: solar array or radioisotope power source
descent shaft, winch or hopper for lava-tube access

subsystems.name: Earth-side mirror
subsystems.role: the reference copy that makes the off-world archive useful rather than merely symbolic.

buildSteps.title: Select and survey a site
buildSteps.detail: Orbital radar, thermal mapping and gravity data are used to find either a permanently shadowed polar cold trap, where temperatures fall to a few tens of kelvin, or a lava tube with a collapsed skylight. A precursor lander then measures the local temperature, radiation dose, dust and rock stability.

buildSteps.title: Prove the vault can be reached
buildSteps.detail: Before any samples leave Earth, a rover descends through the skylight or drills into the shadowed terrain to confirm the chamber is accessible, stable and cold enough at depth.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the chamber
buildSteps.detail: Robots level and line the chosen space, install insulated storage modules and route power and data cabling. The structure is deliberately simple, because repairs are rare and expensive.

buildSteps.title: Prepare and load samples on Earth
buildSteps.detail: Cells and tissues are treated with cryoprotectants and vitrified — cooled fast enough that ice crystals never form — while seeds, spores and some small invertebrates are dried instead. Each sample goes into a sealed ampoule, is pre-cooled, and is loaded into a carrier that holds temperature through launch.

buildSteps.title: Launch and land
buildSteps.detail: Carriers fly as a dedicated payload, typically over a low-energy trajectory to reduce propellant, and land close to the vault site.

buildSteps.title: Transfer and seal
buildSteps.detail: A robotic system moves each ampoule from the lander into the vault racks through a sealed port, so it never warms above its storage temperature or meets outside dust.

buildSteps.title: Commission and baseline
buildSteps.detail: Temperature, pressure and radiation are logged, sample positions recorded, and a small subset returned or tested to confirm viability after the trip.

buildSteps.title: Operate and expand
buildSteps.detail: The archive is serviced robotically every few years, with a viability test of a few samples and replenishment from Earth populations, so the archive tracks a living, changing biosphere rather than freezing one moment.

prerequisites.why: seed banks and medical cell repositories already store material at liquid-nitrogen temperatures, around 77 K; the limit is that most complex organisms cannot yet be revived from stored cells.
dry shippers keep clinical samples cold for days, but nothing has kept a large biological payload cold across an interplanetary transfer.
a vault in permanent shadow gets no sunlight, so it needs a power source and a data link placed on nearby lit terrain.

prerequisites.tech: Subsurface access to lava tubes or shadowed terrain
prerequisites.why: no mission has yet entered a lunar lava tube or drilled into polar cold-trap regolith.
manipulators, lubricants and electronics behave differently at a few tens of kelvin, and repairs are impossible once sealed.

prerequisites.tech: Techniques to rebuild organisms from stored material
prerequisites.why: an archive preserves genomes, not ecosystems; without revival methods it is a record rather than a backup.

pathway.milestone: Earth-based redundancy: national seed vaults and cryobanks, plus remote cold storage such as the Svalbard Global Seed Vault
pathway.unlocks: a working template for sample preparation, sealing and passive cold storage.

pathway.milestone: orbital or lunar-surface demonstration vault holding a small, well-characterised sample set with passive cooling
pathway.unlocks: proof that samples survive launch, landing and years of unattended storage.

pathway.milestone: a subsurface vault inside a lunar lava tube or polar cold trap at meaningful scale
pathway.unlocks: radiation shielding and natural cold that make century-scale storage plausible without continuous power.

pathway.milestone: a network of archives at several off-world sites, paired with revival biology on Earth
pathway.unlocks: genuine redundancy for the biosphere's genetic heritage rather than a single point of failure.
